finalText:
**Merge** combines two branches and keeps both histories intact — it creates a commit that says "I joined these two together." **Rebase** replays your commits on top of the other branch, rewriting them as if you'd made them after the latest changes. The result is a straight line instead of branching lines.

**Use merge** when you're integrating into a shared branch (main, develop) or working with teammates — it's safer and shows when things came together. **Use rebase** for your own branches before pushing — it keeps your personal history clean and linear. Never rebase something already pushed and shared; that rewrites history for everyone.

One practical take: rebase locally to tidy up your work, merge when you're ready to integrate into shared branches. Most teams default to merge to keep the safety margin.
